subject.title: Codex app-server client closes before long maintenance turn completes; Gateway restart also terminates active turn without graceful recovery

question: For Codex-backed channel turns interrupted by Gateway restart or app-server client close after possible side effects, should OpenClaw resume, synthesize a final status, or fail closed with restart-specific recovery guidance?
rationale: Current source has partial retry and restart-marker mechanisms, but the remaining behavior crosses replay safety, transport failure classification, Gateway lifecycle, and channel delivery policy.

options.title: Design restart-aware recovery
options.body: Define a single cross-surface policy for Gateway-shutdown interruption, unexpected app-server close, safe resume, and final user-visible follow-up, then implement it with focused tests.

options.title: Limit to diagnostics and copy
options.body: Keep runtime behavior fail-closed but make user-facing messages and logs distinguish Gateway restart from unexpected app-server failure.

options.title: Wait for live reproduction
options.body: Keep the issue under needs-live-repro until a current-main live run proves the remaining long-maintenance failure path.

recommendation.title: Design restart-aware recovery
recommendation.body: Define a single cross-surface policy for Gateway-shutdown interruption, unexpected app-server close, safe resume, and final user-visible follow-up, then implement it with focused tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The current Codex app-server retry boundary and user-facing failure copy trace to their merged work, making them the best available routing owner for the product choice.
